_comment: Light fixtures and their switches. Units: DECIMAL FEET, same frame as floorplan.json.
_why: Lighting is defined as data for the same reason the walls are: horror events need to address lights by name and by group ('turn off everything downstairs', 'the porch light is on again'), and that is only possible if every fixture has a stable identity rather than being a hand-placed object someone renamed.
_kelvin: Colour temperature in kelvin. Domestic bulbs are 2400-3000K and read as warm and yellow; 4000K+ reads as institutional and is deliberately reserved for the garage and laundry, where it feels colder and less welcoming than the rest of the house.
_intensity: Unity light intensity. Values here are tuned for a dark scene - the house should be lit in pools with real darkness between them, not evenly flooded. Raising these to make the house readable is almost always the wrong fix; raise the Moonlight or the grade's post-exposure instead.
_groups: A switch toggles a GROUP, not a fixture, so one switch can control several lights. Big rooms get two fittings that share a group, so they are lit from both ends but still have exactly one switch. Open-plan neighbours (kitchen + dining, entry + mud hall, mudroom + laundry) share a group too, so the house has 15 switches rather than one per room.
_twoFittings: Rooms over roughly 12 ft in their long dimension (Great Room, Kitchen, Master Bedroom, Master Bath, Garage, Hall) get two fittings, each at lower intensity than a lone fitting would be. Everything else keeps one.

_switchesComment: Switches sit on a wall inside the room at 4'-0", the standard height. 'controls' is a group name from above.
_switchPlacement: Every one of these was derived from where the DOOR actually is. A switch belongs on solid wall, beside the door you enter by, on the latch side so the opening door does not sweep across it.
_consolidated: Was 19 switches, one per room. Now 15, and only where a room genuinely needs its own: Dining shares the kitchen switch, MudHall shares the entry switch, Laundry shares the mudroom switch, and the master closet shares the master bedroom switch.
